per_object_cap.notes: Up to 20 GBs of output from a Notebook may be saved to disk in /kaggle/working. This data is saved automatically and you can then reuse that data in any future Notebook

retention.stated: A Notebook version is a snapshot of your work including your compiled code, log files, output files, data sources, and more.
retention.notes: Additional scratchpad disk space (outside /kaggle/working) that will not be saved outside of the current session

egress.terms: Public dataset/notebook downloads are served without auth and without a published egress meter.

interface_detail: This is a command-line interface tool for interacting via commands in a terminal or shell script
tooling: `kaggle` CLI + REST API (`/api/v1/datasets/download/...`, `/api/v1/kernels/output/...`); `kagglehub` Python client. No rclone backend, but the CLI is scriptable and gsutil-style uploads work through the API.
chaining: As outlined above, in addition to uploading files from your local machine, you can also create Datasets from various data sources including GitHub, remote URLs (any public file hosted on the web), and Notebook output files.
limits_note: 12 h session for CPU/GPU notebooks, 9 h for TPU; output only auto-saves to /kaggle/working when you 'Save & Run All'; scratch space outside /kaggle/working dies with the session; 50 top-level files per dataset.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'iaas'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

reliability_note: Notebook output survives session end as a versioned artifact. The closest thing here to real object storage. But it is write-once per version, and you cannot run a listener (no inbound ports, no server).
confidence_note: The Kaggle notebooks documentation was read on 2026-11-09 and states the auto-saved disk space per Notebook editing session.
